chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woman who makes up for the month of Ramadan, and her husband coerces her to break the fast, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting for him to coerce her after the decline of the sun (midday).'
ai.seo_question: Can a husband force his wife to break her makeup fast for Ramadan after midday?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the interplay between a wife's personal religious obligation (*Qada*) and her husband's marital authority (*Wilayah*). The ruling that coercion is improper after *Zawal* (midday) highlights the distinction between the validity of the fast and the husband's right to manage household affairs, a key point in Shia fiqh regarding the independence of a woman's worship from her husband's control.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Al Husayn Bin Usman, from Sama’at, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the woman who makes up for a Month of Ramazan, but her husband coerces her upon the breaking. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not befitting for him that he coerces her after the (start of the) decline of the sun’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Husayn ibn ‘Uthman from Sama‘ah, from abu Basir who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who fasts as Qada’ (compensatory fast) for the fast of the month of Ramadan and her husband forces her to invalidate her fast. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not proper for him to do so after Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime)/”
